title: UI/UX issue with restricted.networks.access
description:
### Please confirm

- [x] I have searched existing issues to check if an issue already exists for the bug I encountered.

### Distribution

Ubuntu

### Distribution version

22.04

```shell
N/A
```

### Output of "lxc info" or system info if it fails

```shell
$ lxc version
Client version: 5.21.4 LTS
Server version: 5.21.4 LTS
```

### Issue description

Removing an existing network from restricted.networks.access prevents project deletion, but hides the "offending" network

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a project
2. Allow two networks in `restricted.networks.access` (`networkA` and `networkB`).
3. Create a network `networkA` in the project.
4. Remove `networkA` from `restricted.networks.access`, so the value is now just `networkB`.
5. Try to delete the project

Deleting errors out with `Error: Only empty projects can be removed`.
`lxc project show` will show that the project is used by `networkA`, but `lxc network show --project $project networkA` will say `Network not found`, same when trying to delete. If you want to be able to see/delete that network, you need to add it back to `restricted.networks.access`.

LXD probably shouldn't allow removing an existing network from `restricted.networks.access`
